answer: Public inference-service proof: each epoch every agent must answer twenty prompts sent by strangers to its endpoint, bending like a willow to real demand. Three random peers score each reply for quality and latency and post the scores at the agent's vertex in the service graph; identical or empty replies quarantine the identity and freeze rewards three epochs. Faking 1,000 endpoints needs 1,000 GPU instances, about $12,000 a month, while one honest agent answers twenty prompts in minutes on the model it already runs and pays nothing extra — a walnut of real work no script can crack for free.
